title: Val's in the Alley jam sessions in Cleveland
summary: With Prince Robinson, Joe, Clyde Hart and Lannie Scott, Roy jammed with Tatum in Cleveland during the hard Cotton Pickers days.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Yeah, that's when he was on the radio.
Yeah! And we used to wait. We used to go to Val's In The Alley... Were you there the night that Skippy Williams was there?

He said he had the... No, he didn't have no job there. Shit. Heh-heh. It was me, Prince Robinson... Now, there was a helluva clarinet player. Boy, did people sleep on that... That cat was a living (?) on clarinet! Prince, Joe, myself and Clyde Hart, and Lannie Scott used to all go there, you know. If they had a new piano player around or something, they'd always let me start off -- because I used to play a pretty good stride in those days, you know. I'd start off, and like the cat would stand there listening, he said, 'Oh shit.' But I got the shit going, you know. But they didn't like to hear all that, you know. When I'd get ready to quit, I would take it and Clyde would take it, and he would stretch out, you know, then Lannie Scott would take it, then he would stretch, then I would wrap it up, boy. And when I got done, that fellow had

turned his head...he was gonna pee in his drawers, you know. We used to think up some nice little head arrangements. Too bad they didn't have tape recorders in those days. We got some nice little things going there, you know.

Yeah, Art used to take us in... Things was pretty bad for us with the Cotton-Pickers, you know. We'd wait on Art, and then after we'd get through jammin' we'd go next door, they had a little diner, and they had this pigfeet and beans -- red beans. It was good! Yeah, I used to swing on the swing porch, you know...
